newsitem.title: USA: Cato adds president title to COO John Cato.
newsitem.headline: Cato adds president title to COO John Cato.

text.p: Cato Corp, reporting a rising net income for the second quarter, gave vice-chairman and chief operating officer John Cato the additional title of president.
A company spokesman was not immediately available to say who -- if anybody -- Cato replaces.
The apparel specialty retailer posted net income of $3.8 million, or $0.13 a share, in the quarter ended August 2. This compared with net of $2.4 million or $0.08 a share, in the 1996 quarter.
A May 20 First Call poll of seven analysts had put Cato's earnings at $0.10 a share.

"Both divisions experienced same-stores growth above plan on inventory levels flat with plan and last year," said chief executive Wayland Cato in a statement. "Merchandise margin did not achieve last year's levels due to a planned decrease in our initial mark-up."
The retailer's stock hit a new 52-week high of 8-1/8 Monday and traded at 8 by mid-morning, up 1/4.
